11. The Petitioner has submitted that as per the IA dated 30.3.2021, the transmission 
asset was scheduled to be commissioned by 29 months from the date of the IA, which

13. MSEDCL, in its reply and written submission, has submitted as under:  
a. The Petitioner has claimed the COD of the transmission asset as 30.8.2023 
on the basis of successful trial operations, however, the absence of power flow 
confirms that the project was not operational and the transmission asset which 
was to be commissioned by MUML, was incomplete and the said transmission 
line was commissioned only in September 2024, and the delay was due to the 
delay caused in the associated transmission sy stem. In any circumstances, 
the beneficiaries, including MSEDCL, herein, should not be made liable for the

transmission charges prior to the actual power flow. Reliance has been placed 
on the order dated 16.5.2024 in the Petition No. 180/TT/2021, passed by the 
Commission, wherein the pleadings qua the tariff charges for the period from 
the date of trial operations to the actual date of commissioning of the 
associated transmission line were not considered. The relevant extract is  as 
under: 
“15. Without going into the merits of the claims of the Petitioner for approval of the 
COD of the transmission asset as 13.5.2019, condonation of the time over-run, cost 
over-run and the sharing of the transmission charges, and the objections raised by 
MMPCL, M SEDCL, and MSETCL in the instant petition, we hereby direct the 
petitioner in the exercise of regulatory power to file a fresh petition within 60 days of 
COD of the above-referred transmission elements, i.e., A(i), A(ii) and A(iii) under the 
scope of MUML and the declaration of the COD of the transmission asset. The 
Respondents are at liberty to raise their concerns in the said petition. The Petitioner’s 
claims and the Respondent’s objections, if any, will be dealt with as per the 
applicable regulations.” 
 
b. The absence of the established power flow confirms that the transmission 
project was not operational, which is quite evident that the transmission service 
was yet to be provided and the Project, which was not available for use by the 
beneficiaries, till September 2024.  
 
14. MPPMCL, in its reply, has submitted as under: 
a. The absence of established power flow confirms that the project covered under 
the Petition was not operational , and evidently, the transmission service was 
not provided and the Project , which was not available for use by the 
beneficiaries, till the 31.3.2024.  
b. The Hon’ble Supreme Court vide judgment dated 3.3.2016 in Civil Appeal No. 
9193 of 2012, in the case of PGCIL vs. PSPCL & Ors., reported as (2016) 4 
SCC 797, has  inter-alia, held that the COD of the transmission lines can be

Order in Petition No. 149/TT/2024 Page 11 of 97 
  
achieved only on the fulfilment of certain conditions. The relevant para of the 
judgment is reproduced as under: 
“7. The language in the above definition is clear and unambiguous. We agree 
with the Tribunal that COD of  transmission lines can be achieved only on 
fulfilment of following three conditions: 
 
(i) The line has been charged successfully 
(ii) Its trial operation has been successfully carried out, and  
(iii) It is in regular service.” 
However, the instant case does not fulfil the afore-stated conditions. 
 
c. Further, the Hon’ble Supreme Court vide judgment dated 3.3.2016, has also held 
that until the power flows from the transmission system, the beneficiaries should 
not be burdened with the tariff. The relevant par a of the said judgment is 
reproduced herein as under: 
“13. Since we are in  agreement with the Tribunal that in the present case, 
Respondent No. 1 and the beneficiaries could not have been made liable to 
pay the tariff before the transmission line was operational, we find no infirmity 
in the impugned order. Therefore, the appeals are liabl e to be dismissed. 
Accordingly, both the appeals are dismissed without prejudice to the right of 
the Appellant, if any, available to it under law, against NTPC. There shall be 
no order as to costs.” 
 
d. Under no circumstances should the beneficiaries, including MPPMCL, be made 
liable to bear the transmission charges of the bays covered under the Petition prior 
to the actual power flow, which had not taken place till 31.3.2024 . Therefore, the 
liability to pay the transmission charges for such prior period under the guise of the 
COD would be contrary to the law as settled on the issue by the Hon’ble Supreme 
Court, as referred herein above and , therefore, cannot be fastened to the 
beneficiaries. Accordingly, the liability, if any, to pay the transmission charges with 
respect to the aforesaid line bays covered under the instant Petition, before the

Order in Petition No. 149/TT/2024 Page 12 of 97 
  
actual power flow through them , should not be imposed on the beneficiaries, 
including MPPMCL. 
 
15. MUML, in its reply and written submissions, has submitted as under: 
a. The Petitioner cannot claim the proposed COD in terms of Regulation 5(2) of 
the 2019 Tariff Regulations, prior to the commissioning of the PK Line , which 
is 24.8.2024 (Original SCOD of PK Line was 22.12.2023, which was extended 
by virtue of the order of the Ministry of Power  (MoP) and Force Majeure 
events). Therefore, the instant Petition is misconceived and ought to be 
rejected.  
b. The Petitioner has not complied with the requirements of Regulation 5(2) of 
the 2019 Tariff Regulations. In particular, the Petitioner has not provided 
sufficient notice of at least one month regarding the commissioning of the 
transmission asset to MUML. 
c. In terms of Regulation 5(2) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations, a transmission 
licensee is only entitled to declare the COD when its transmission 
system/element is ready, but the interconnected transmission system is not 
ready as per its agreed project impleme ntation schedule. In Regulation 5(2), 
as extracted hereinabove, the reference to the term 'agreed project 
implementation schedule’ of the other transmission licensee makes it clear that 
the COD of the Petitioner cannot be before the SCOD of the inter -connecting 
transmission licensee. As per Regulation 5(2) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations, 
the impacted transmission licensee has no locus to declare its deemed COD 
as a date before the SCOD of the interconnected transmission system.

d. Accordingly, the approval of the proposed COD, as claimed by the Petitioner, 
cannot be accepted by the Commission as the same are in clear contravention 
of Regulation 5(2) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations. The agreed SCOD of the PK 
Line, only on account of the MoP orders, is 22.8.2024. Therefore, PGCIL 
cannot seek COD prior to 22.8.2024. 
e. The Petitioner’s claim that the commissioning of the transmission asset is on 
30.8.2023 is wrong and denied as the same are in violation and contrary to 
Regulation 5(2) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations and not in line with the MUML's 
TSA and contrary to various orders passed by the Commission time to time. 
f. The Petitioner is trying to mislead the Commission by referring to the minutes 
of the meeting dated 3.11.2022. In the same minutes of the meeting dated 
3.11.2022, it was clearly mention ed that the date shall be subject to 
modifications based on the progress of the MUML Project. Pertinently, the CEA 
in its MoM specified that SCOD may be finalized at a later stage, if all parties 
agree. 
g. The SCOD decided  upon and contemplated in the minutes of the meeting 
dated 27.11.2020 were not final and subject to further revision based on the 
progress of the PK Line and once a final date was agreed by the parties as per 
the mechanism provided in the MoP policy dated 15.7.2015 and the TSA. 
h. The Petitioner is trying to mislead the Commission by referring to the letters 
dated 24.6.2020 and 8.9.2020 and the MoM dated 27.11.2020. The Petitioner 
has not placed on record the subsequent communication dated 28.12.2022 
issued by the MoP to the CEA and other stakeholders , recognising the

Order in Petition No. 149/TT/2024 Page 14 of 97 
  
expected COD for the MUML Project in June 2024. The commissioning dates 
of the said meeting dated 27.11.2020 were indicated considering the progress 
of the PK Line at that time, and the MoM clearly provided that such date shall 
be subject to  modifications based o n the progress of the PK Line. The early 
commissioning was never finalized and acted upon by the stakeholders as per 
the mechanism prescribed by the MoP Policy. Since the above-stated 
mechanism was not acted upon by the stakeholders, the SCOD was never 
postponed. 
16. The Petitioner , in its rejoinder to the reply of MSEDCL  and MPPMCL, has

transmission element to be developed by the other transmission licensee has not been 
commissioned. Accordingly, the  Petitioner has claimed the COD for the transmission 
asset under Regulation 5(2) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations.  
 
17. Further, the Petitioner, in its rejoinder to the reply of MUML, has submitted that the 
Petitioner’s assets were scheduled to be commissioned on 30.8.2023, and accordingly , 
the Petitioner commissioned its scope of work on 30.8.2023. The Petitioner achieved the

asset could not be utilized despite its commissioning due to the delay in the completion/

reasons not attributable to itself. The Petitioner has submitted that the contention raised

the readiness of its scope of works. As the inter-connecting transmission line in the scope

contesting that commissioning dates in the aforementioned meetings were indicated 
considering the progress of the PK Line at that time, and the MoM clearly provide that 
such dates shall be subject to  modifications based o n the progress of the PK Line , is

dated 3.11.2020 reveals that the SCOD of the line bays and inter-connecting transmission

was contingent on the project’s progress. This shift in stance disregards the collaborative 
efforts and mutual decisions documented in  the coordination meetings, reflecting an 
imprudent approach tha t undermines the integrity of the process.  It is evident from the 
monthly progress report of the CEA that MUML has communicated August 2023 as its 
SCOD till March 2022 , and it was only from April  2022 onwards  that the expected 
commissioning date was communicated as December 2023. Further, the reliance placed

that case is different from the present case.”

21. Regulation 5 of the 2019 Tariff Regulations provides as under: 
“5. Date of Commercial Operation:  (1) The date of commercial operation of a 
generating station or unit thereof or a transmission system or element thereof and 
associated communication system shall be determined in accordance with the provisions 
of the Grid Code. 
 
(2) In case the transmission system or element thereof executed by a transmission

the transmission system of other transmission licensee as per the agreed project 
implementation schedule is not ready for commercial operation, the transmission 
licensee may file petition before the Commission for approval of the date of commercial 
operation of such transmission system or element thereof: 
 Provided that the transmission licensee seeking the approval of the date of 
commercial operation under this clause shall give prior notice of at least one month, to 
the generating company or the other transmission licensee and the long-term customers 
of its transmission system, as the case may be, regarding the date of commercial 
operation:

commercial operation of the transmission system under this clause shall be required to

(a) Energisation certificate issued by the Regional Electrical Inspector under Central

(b) Trial operation certificate issue d by the concerned RLDC for charging element with

(c) Implementation Agreement, if any, executed by the parties;
